task.name: Semantic readiness requirement is operator policy under intake.semantic_review and defaults to off
task.story_text:
## What
Semantic readiness becomes operator policy. A single mode under the existing `intake` config, `intake.semantic_review: off | required`, decides whether a ratified semantic review is required before an implementation-ready issue is admitted. The default is `off`, and a `forge.yaml` with no such key means `off`. When off, no consumer of semantic readiness evaluates, spends, or withholds. When `required`, the contract shipped by #2785 applies unchanged: sprint entry evaluates once per revision, admission consumes only an operator ratification, and every concern is decided with `forge ratify-semantic`. The evaluator and its records stay available on demand through `forge review-semantic` in either mode.

## Why
The ratified-readiness contract (#2785, in the runtime since v0.16.0rc15) requires a review for every `bug`, `enhancement`, `task` and `spike` in the `implementation_ready` state, with no configuration and no `--force` path. Since #2966 (rc18) sprint entry runs the evaluation itself. The effect on the operator, measured on 2026-09-09 (sprint `245fa4769933`): every implementation-ready issue in the sprint was withheld with `semantic_review_not_ratified`; three evaluations spent $0.46 outside `--budget`, reported after the fact; the refusal carried no finding text, so deciding each one meant reading `.forge/audits/semantic-review/records.jsonl` or asking another agent; ratification is one issue per command; and an edit to a body retires the ratification, so a corrected issue stops again. Of the three concerns raised, one was a real arithmetic error in the body, and two were false positives an evaluator that reads only the issue body cannot avoid: a dependency it could not see was transitively declared, and an "Independence note" the diagnosis renderer inserts mechanically. A clean evaluation still needs an empty ratification before the story can run.

The milestone this contract belongs to is "capture → shaped → groomed → ready without operator keystrokes." As shipped, the gate adds at least one keystroke per issue per revision on every project running this rc, including the live adopter. The ADR-0009 as-built text says the policy half was split from the evaluator "so the policy could be decided against measurements rather than ahead of them." No checked-in corpus report or recorded measurement decision was found; the store holds six evaluations. Defaulting to `off` restores that sequencing: the evaluator keeps recording where an operator asks for it, and the requirement is switched on per project when the measurement supports it. This is the smallest change that stops the withholding. The redesign the measurement may justify later (findings presented inline at the refusal, batch ratification, spend inside the declared budget, no ratification of an empty concern set) is deferred, not decided here.

## Acceptance criteria
- `intake.semantic_review` accepts `off` and `required`, defaults to `off`, and a configuration with no such key behaves as `off`. Any other value is a configuration error reported at load, not a silent fallback.
- When the mode is `off`, semantic readiness is `not_required` for every document regardless of type or lifecycle state, and every consumer of the readiness state honours that: query-issue sprint admission, manifest sprint admission, `forge status --ready`, and the dispatch-time revision check. None of them runs the evaluator, spends, or withholds a story on semantic grounds; a story that would otherwise be admitted is admitted.
- When the mode is `required`, behaviour is exactly the #2785 contract as documented in `docs/reference/semantic-readiness.md`; nothing about ratification, revision identity, or the reason codes changes.
- `forge review-semantic` and `forge ratify-semantic` work in both modes and record on the same terms, so an operator can evaluate and ratify on demand without switching the gate on.
- The ADR-0009 "As built (slice 6)" section is amended to state that the requirement is operator policy defaulting to off, so the ADR no longer says policy requires a review for the four implementation types unconditionally. `docs/reference/semantic-readiness.md` and the `forge.yaml` reference document the key and its default.
- Existing recorded evaluations and ratifications keep their meaning: switching from `off` to `required` on a project whose issues already carry a ratified clean revision reports those revisions `reviewed_ready` without re-evaluation.

## Example
```
forge.yaml (no intake.semantic_review key)

  sprint admission for #2951:
  ✓ ADMIT   #2951  shape runnable · semantic review not required (intake.semantic_review: off)

forge.yaml
  intake:
    semantic_review: required

  sprint admission for #2951:
  ⊘ #2951  semantic_review_not_ratified  [awaiting_ratification]  1 concern — run `forge ratify-semantic 2951`
```

Note: developer handoff says gate BLOCKED but the coordinator-verified authoritative gate verdict for 95bb9c94 is PASS; I relied on the verified PASS.

findings.description: A forge.yaml containing the unquoted key value semantic_review: off — exactly as shown in the docs/guides/inputs-reference.md example block — is parsed by yaml.safe_load into boolean False (verified: the loader at load.py:1126 uses PyYAML safe_load, and safe_load('semantic_review: off') yields False under the YAML 1.1 resolver), which then fails the membership check against the string set and aborts configuration loading with a ValueError, so a project explicitly writing the documented default cannot load its config at all.

finding_registry.description: A forge.yaml containing the unquoted key value semantic_review: off — exactly as shown in the docs/guides/inputs-reference.md example block — is parsed by yaml.safe_load into boolean False (verified: the loader at load.py:1126 uses PyYAML safe_load, and safe_load('semantic_review: off') yields False under the YAML 1.1 resolver), which then fails the membership check against the string set and aborts configuration loading with a ValueError, so a project explicitly writing the documented default cannot load its config at all.
A forge.yaml containing intake.semantic_review: no or intake.semantic_review: false loads successfully as semantic_review off.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

steps.description: Define and validate the operator policy.
steps.details: Add `semantic_review` to the existing `IntakeConfig`, default it to `off`, parse it from `intake`, and reject values other than `off` and `required` during config load. Cover absent, explicit valid, and invalid values.

steps.description: Make semantic requirement derivation policy-aware while retaining revision-scoped evaluation state.
steps.details: Thread the configured mode through the existing `semantic_requirement`, readiness derivations, automatic evaluation, query admission, manifest admission, ready-queue reporting, re-admitted issue handling, and dispatch revision check. In `off`, derive `not_required` without evaluation or withholding; in `required`, retain the current automatic evaluation, ratification, reason-code, and revision-identity behavior.

steps.description: Prove policy behavior at the semantic and command seams.
steps.details: Update existing required-policy assertions to select `required`, and add coverage that `off` admits otherwise runnable issues without evaluator calls or dispatch withholding across query, manifest, ready-queue, and revision-check seams. Verify on-demand review and ratification still persist records in both modes, and a clean ratification recorded while off becomes `reviewed_ready` after switching to required.

criteria_mapping.criterion: intake.semantic_review accepts off and required, defaults to off, and a configuration with no such key behaves as off. Any other value is a configuration error reported at load, not a silent fallback.

When the mode is off, semantic readiness is not_required for every document regardless of type or lifecycle state, and every consumer of the readiness state honours that: query-issue sprint admission, manifest sprint admission, forge status --ready, and the dispatch-time revision check. None of them runs the evaluator, spends, or withholds a story on semantic grounds; a story that would otherwise be admitted is admitted.
When the mode is required, behaviour is exactly the #2785 contract as documented in docs/reference/semantic-readiness.md; nothing about ratification, revision identity, or the reason codes changes.
forge review-semantic and forge ratify-semantic work in both modes and record on the same terms, so an operator can evaluate and ratify on demand without switching the gate on.

Existing recorded evaluations and ratifications keep their meaning: switching from off to required on a project whose issues already carry a ratified clean revision reports those revisions reviewed_ready without re-evaluation.
